headline: Microsoft reportedly training salespeople to talk down OpenAI and Anthropic
summary: A new report suggests Microsoft is coaching its sales team to negatively compare its AI products to rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic, highlighting its own models' efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
details: Microsoft is reportedly prepping its sales team for a more competitive stance in the AI industry. An internal meeting outlined a plan for salespeople to negatively compare AI products from companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to Microsoft's own offerings.

The strategy session, focused on the new fiscal year, emphasized pitching the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of Microsoft’s in-house models. Executive VP Jay Parikh reportedly stated, "Everyone else is selling parts — we’re selling the full end-to-end system."

Executive VP Jacob Andreou reportedly presented a direct comparison between Copilot and Anthropic’s Claude. He noted that within Microsoft’s office apps, Anthropic’s model was "slower and less accurate, and lacked the proper security integrations."

This move is particularly notable given Microsoft's long-standing dependence on these same companies for the AI models powering its products. TechCrunch has reached out to Microsoft and Anthropic for comment.

Earlier reports indicated Microsoft has been replacing OpenAI and Anthropic models in flagship apps like Word and Excel with its own, citing cost-cutting as a primary reason. This new sales strategy aligns with that shift.

The revised partnership with OpenAI in April, which dropped the exclusivity clause, may also explain the new competitive pitch. Microsoft is reportedly seeking to bolster investor confidence amid questions about its significant AI business investments.

headline_marked: [[Running Gemma 4 26B on a 13-Year-Old Xeon]]: Practical AI Performance Without GPUs
headline: Running Gemma 4 26B on a 13-Year-Old Xeon: Practical AI Performance Without GPUs
summary: A new tutorial demonstrates how to run the Gemma 4 26B LLM on a 13-year-old Xeon CPU, reducing RAM usage from 120GB to ~40GB and achieving AI inference at ~15% of typical GPU costs.
details: Large language models like Gemma 4 26B typically demand powerful GPUs with high VRAM. A new tutorial demonstrates how to run this 26B parameter model on a 13-year-old Intel Xeon E5 v2 series processor using CPU-only optimization techniques.

This approach utilizes model quantization and memory-efficient execution, drastically reducing RAM usage from 120GB (float16) to approximately 40GB. This enables practical AI inference on legacy hardware at roughly 15% of the cost of GPU-based solutions.

While modern GPUs offer superior throughput (100-300 tokens/sec), this CPU-only method is ideal for edge deployments or proof-of-concept work. For production workloads requiring higher throughput, upgrading to Xeon Scalable (2nd Gen) is recommended.
